meta.title: iAguide
meta.description: A visual course on how AI actually works: tokens and attention, agent harnesses, training and reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, quantization, and the memory that holds a thought in flight.

home.title: iAguide
home.promise: {count} modules on how AI actually works — the tokens under the words, the loop around the weights, the arithmetic of training, and the memory bus that decides how fast you think.
home.outcomesTitle: What you will be able to do
outcomes: Pick a model from its card and its numbers, not from a vibe.
Read Q4_K_M, NF4, MXFP4 and predict what each one costs you.
See an agent harness as a loop you can debug, not a chat box.
Size a machine: parameters, KV cache, bandwidth, context.
Know when LoRA is worth it — and when it is a distraction.
Tell prefill from decode when something is slow.
Build a twenty-case eval before you build a demo.
Spot a prompt injection in text your agent is about to read.
home.layersLede: Almost every confusion about AI is a layer confusion. Somebody blames the model for a harness bug, or the harness for a memory bandwidth wall. The course is built so you always know which floor you are standing on.

layers.name: The harness
layers.blurb: Prompts, tools, threads, caches, permissions. Written by humans, in ordinary code. Where most bugs live.

layers.name: The model
layers.blurb: A few hundred billion numbers and one operation: score every next token. Trained, not programmed.

layers.name: The silicon
layers.blurb: Weights must be read to be used. Memory size decides what fits; bandwidth decides how fast it thinks.

home.tracksLede: Walk them in order or jump to the one you came for. Every module names its prerequisites.
home.startLede: No account, no telemetry, no upsell. Both languages are written, not machine-translated — switch at any point and keep your place.
home.openLede: MIT licensed and built to be forked. A module is a folder: metadata, two lessons, one diagram. Add yours.
